'Make for yourself two trumpets of silver' — the Sifrei: trumpets are needed even though 9:23 moves the camp by the Word (two verses, both kept); 'for yourself' from what is yours; TWO — not more, not less, alike in look, height and beauty; 'beaten' a solid bar; the two offices — calling the congregation, journeying the camps (the clause's one seat); both trumpets for the congregation, one for the princes — to the door by induction (I3), and the princes addressed first everywhere (Num 30:2); THE INK: the trumpet-word spelled three ways in the chapter (10:2; 10:8-9; 10:10 — computed), the construct 'two of' the parser's gap again (10:2 → []), Onkelos writing the two ('two trumpets') and 'drawn' for beaten.
middah: ink (the three spellings and the parser's gap computed; the Sifrei's fixed count read as it stands)

claim_en: TEKIAH AND TERUAH ARE TWO SOUNDS; TEKIAH-TERUAH-TEKIAH; ROSH HASHANAH BY THE IDENTITY; THE TERUAH IS A WAIL. From 10:7 'blow, and not a teruah' the plain sound and the broken sound are distinct; tekiah precedes ('blow a teruah'), a tekiah follows — from the superfluous 'SECOND' of 10:6 as a prototype (I3); and Rosh Hashanah by 'teruah' here / 'teruah' there (I2): tekiah-teruah-tekiah for the day's three written teruot — nine sounds, the Torah's and the scribes' split a two-setting parameter (the exam's Rosh Hashanah 33b-34a); the north and the west one set or three (73:3); the assembly with tekiah only (74:1). THE INK: the blow-verb eight tokens and the teruah-word five in 10:3-10 (computed); Onkelos renders the teruah as a WAIL at 10:5, 10:7, 10:9 (cut from the shelf's bytes) — the very rendering the exam uses to fix the sound (Rosh Hashanah 33b on the Targum of Judg 5:28): the translation layer load-bearing again.
middah: I2 (the identity 'teruah'/'teruah' carrying the desert's blasts to Rosh Hashanah; I3 on 'second' in the note)

Tarfon) or whole only (R. Akiva — 'priests'/'priests' with Lev 3:2, I2); R. Tarfon's TESTIMONY — his lame uncle blowing — answered by R. Akiva: on Rosh Hashanah or the Jubilee's Yom Kippur, the shofar, not the trumpets — 'Tarfon saw and forgot; Akiva expounded of himself and matched the halakhah': a witnessed memory yields to a derivation that reconstructs the forgotten day (the tradition's own memory failure and repair, as at Shevuot 20b); 'for YOU a statute forever' (the clause with its lamed one seat — computed) — a statute, not an heirloom: every vessel Moses made served the generations EXCEPT the trumpets (the exam's Menachot 28b).
